report:
Reviewed the entire browser_rust_source claim and both registered entries. The only associated implementation is the explicit region surrounding todo::browser_source_pane_preserves_context_and_provenance in spec_plan.rs; the only associated test is that same assertion-free function. Both are TODO, with an explanation naming show/hide, navigation, multiple sites, missing source, declaration ranges, cfg, markers and snapshot labels. It is not executable behavioral proof and does not establish completed implementation. No ordinary or N/A evidence is registered.

To assess the deferral against current work, captured and inspected browser.rs, web/browser.js, web/index.html and the first 135 lines of browser.test.cjs. Existing foundations are substantial: browser.rs source_data imports indexed correspondence locations and source files into serialized snapshot data, and render embeds data with the HTML/JS assets. The template provides an initially hidden pane and show/close buttons beside the selected-entity content. JS toggleSource alters pane visibility and aria-expanded without changing the selected route; show clears a prior explicit source choice and refreshes an open pane on navigation. sourceOwner resolves item/method/module/crate and anchor selection, with members showing their owner. renderSourcePane uses the target map, flattens multiple correspondence locations into selectable options and refreshes the chosen site. It reports no available mapping and absent source files separately, shows path/line, renders surrounding full-file source with line numbers, marks line..end_line and scrolls to the declaration. Module markers explicitly disclaim executable coverage; macro-input locations say expanded Rust is absent; cfg conditions are explicitly not evaluated. Snapshot text states when the HTML captured source. These are source-inspected foundations, not a promotion of the registered TODO to complete implementation or evidence that a browser interaction occurred.

Every claim aspect remains in scope of the TODO: preserving selection through reveal/hide; following selection; indexed correspondences; file/numbered surrounding code and declaration highlighting; independent site choice; missing-source feedback; module/macro/cfg provenance versus confirmed execution; source snapshot labeling and avoiding inference that navigation proves execution or a satisfied rule. The deferred validation requires a browser/DOM interaction harness operating on generated indexed snapshots, with multiple sites and module/macro/cfg cases plus missing source and exact line ranges. Such a harness must check route retention and updates, rendered visibility and selection, as well as provenance messages; source-string assertions alone cannot establish that behavior.

The captured JS tests provide useful unregistered partial evidence: they assert actual indexed annotation locations, enum declaration text, data-definition markers, method source ownership, module/macro labels, choosing a second fixture definition and escaped unevaluated cfg text. They also test raw source-route highlighting and escaping, which is distinct from exercising the pane UI. They consume an exported artifact and call pure render functions; they do not drive the DOM toggle/navigation lifecycle or fully assert every missing-source and provenance scenario. Accordingly they are not substituted for the associated TODO, and no complete test coverage or runtime acceptance is claimed. Existing partial source code is captured as contextual dependency rather than relabeled as a completed associated implementation.

No source changes or behavioral reproduction were needed. This review executed only review start/read/record and source inspection; centrally run suites were not rerun and no test execution is claimed here. Dependency capture is complete for this assessment. The explicit implementation-and-test TODO fairly preserves unfinished end-to-end work, with the prerequisite and remaining scenarios explained above. No requested edits.
